name: Louisiana

sales.rateNote: State rate raised from 4.45% to 5% on January 1, 2025 by Act 11 of the 2024 Third Extraordinary Session (the R.S. 47:321.1 levy went from 0.45% to 1%). The 5% rate runs through December 31, 2029; from January 1, 2030 total state levies drop to 4.75%. Parish, municipal and school board taxes come on top.

scheduledChanges.what: Act 11 (2024 3rd Ext. Session): the R.S. 47:321.1 levy falls from 1% to 0.75%, bringing total state sales and use tax to 4.75%.

local.levies: parishes, municipalities, school boards and other local governmental subdivisions, with voter approval; collected locally (not by the Department of Revenue)
local.capNote: Constitution Art. VI, Sec. 29: combined local sales taxes may not exceed 3%, but the legislature may authorize additional local taxes by law, so many areas exceed 3%.

groceries.note: Food for home consumption is exempt from the state sales tax (0% in the R-1002 rate table); the constitutional limit applies only to the state, so parish and municipal sales taxes can still apply to groceries.

clothing.note: Clothing is taxable (listed among items subject to sales and use tax); hunting apparel is exempt only during the Second Amendment Weekend holiday.

otherRates.note: Subject to an additional 5% state tax on top of the general sales tax.

otherRates.item: residential electricity, natural gas and water
otherRates.note: Exempt from state sales tax under Art. VII, Sec. 2.2 of the Constitution.

holidays2026.name: Louisiana Second Amendment Weekend Sales Tax Holiday
holidays2026.items: consumer purchases of firearms, ammunition and hunting supplies (archery items, hunting apparel, hunting knives, optics, etc.); exempt from state and local sales tax

sales.holidayNote: Act 11 of 2024 repealed the annual back-to-school holiday (R.S. 47:305.54) and the hurricane preparedness holiday (R.S. 47:305.58); only the Second Amendment Weekend remains.

useTax.note: For purchases on or after January 1, 2025, individuals pay a flat 9% consumer use tax (5% state + 4% distributed to local governments), regardless of the actual local rate, on the income tax return or Form R-1035.

facts.text: Louisiana's 5% state rate is temporary: Act 11 of 2024 sets it from January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2029, then 4.75% from 2030.
Out-of-state purchases are taxed at a flat 9% consumer use tax (5% state, 4% local) whatever the local rate at home.
The 2024 reform repealed the back-to-school and hurricane preparedness tax holidays; the Second Amendment Weekend (September 4-6 in 2026) survived.
Groceries and prescription drugs are exempt from the state tax, but local parish and city sales taxes can still apply to them.
The Constitution caps combined local sales taxes at 3%, unless the legislature authorizes more by law and voters approve.
Cable and satellite TV are hit with an extra 5% state tax on top of the regular sales tax.

property.levied: parishes, municipalities, school boards, levee and other special districts (plus any state millage); property is valued by the elected parish assessor, reviewed by the parish governing authority and the Louisiana Tax Commission

assessment.text: Assessed value is a fixed percentage of fair market value set by the Constitution: 10% for land and for residential improvements, 15% for electric cooperative property, 25% for public service property (other property 15%). Farm, marsh and timber land is assessed at 10% of use value. Property must be reappraised at least every four years; homestead owners facing a reappraisal increase of more than 50% get a phase-in.

homestead.name: Homestead Exemption
homestead.text: The owner-occupied bona fide homestead (up to 160 acres) is exempt from state, parish and special ad valorem taxes on the first $7,500 of assessed value, which equals $75,000 of market value at the 10% residential assessment ratio. The exemption does not extend to municipal taxes, except municipal school taxes and, in Orleans Parish, general city, school and levee taxes.

otherRelief.name: Special Assessment Level (assessment freeze)
otherRelief.text: Freezes the assessment of a homestead owned by people 65+, veterans with a 50%+ service-connected disability, permanently disabled people and families of service members killed or missing in action. Income limit: federal AGI of $100,000, indexed to CPI from tax year 2026; Acts 2025 No. 220 would raise it to $150,000 from January 1, 2027 if the constitutional amendment is ratified.

facts.text: Louisiana homes are assessed at only 10% of market value, and the homestead exemption removes the first $7,500 of that assessed value.
Farm, marsh and timber land is assessed at 10% of its use value rather than its market value.
If a reappraisal raises a homestead's assessed value by more than 50%, the tax increase is phased in.
Seniors 65+ and certain disabled owners can freeze their home's assessment if their income is under the $100,000 AGI limit (indexed from 2026).
The homestead exemption also covers a mobile home used as the primary residence, even if the owner does not own the land under it.

The LDR Consumer Use Tax web page still shows 8.45%, while the January 2026 Form R-1035 instructions give 9% for purchases from January 1, 2025: the form was followed.
